# Delivery Plan

> **Legend** — `[AI]`: an agent performs the step (the default; unmarked steps are `[AI]`).
> `[HUMAN]`: only a human can do it. `[AI+HUMAN]`: the agent prepares and the human finishes.

This checklist is prospective. It does not authorize implementation, staging, committing, pushing,
opening PRs, or changing either repository. Execute it only after the user explicitly names this
plan for execution.

## Delivery Mode

`worktree-to-pr` applies independently to `ose-public` and `ose-private`. The plan is single-sourced
in public. Each repository has its own worktree, branches, commits, PRs, current-head/base CI,
rules-propagation evidence, recovery proof, merge, and cleanup.

- Private: `R-PRI:worktrees/adopt-beavernest-test-automation/`

```bash
rtk bash -lc 'set -euo pipefail; plan_identity="$(rtk node -e '"'"'const fs=require("node:fs"),path=require("node:path"),cp=require("node:child_process"); const id="adopt-beavernest-test-automation"; const fail=()=>{throw Error("Execution root validation failed; stop and recheck the selected checkouts and Phase 0 evidence")}; const check=x=>{if(!x)fail()}; const real=x=>fs.realpathSync(x); const git=(root,...args)=>cp.execFileSync("git",["-C",root,...args],{encoding:"utf8",stdio:["ignore","pipe","pipe"]}); const text=x=>x.replace(/\n$/,""); const origin=root=>{const raw=text(git(root,"remote","get-url","origin")); let u; try{u=new URL(raw.replace(/^git@github\.com:/,"ssh://git@github.com/"))}catch{fail()} check(["https:","ssh:"].includes(u.protocol)&&u.hostname==="github.com"&&!u.port&&!u.search&&!u.hash); const name=u.pathname.replace(/^\//,"").replace(/\.git\/?$/,"").replace(/\/$/,""); check(["wahidyankf/ose-public","wahidyankf/ose-private"].includes(name)); return name.endsWith("ose-public")?"public":"private"}; const records=root=>git(root,"worktree","list","--porcelain","-z").split("\0\0").filter(Boolean).map(x=>Object.fromEntries(x.split("\0").filter(Boolean).map(l=>{const n=l.indexOf(" ");return n<0?[l,""]:[l.slice(0,n),l.slice(n+1)]}))); const discover=(selected,repo,registered)=>{check(typeof selected==="string"&&selected.length>0&&!/[\r\n\0]/.test(selected)); const common=real(text(git(selected,"rev-parse","--path-format=absolute","--git-common-dir"))); check(path.basename(common)===".git"); const primary=path.dirname(common); check(real(text(git(primary,"rev-parse","--show-toplevel")))===primary&&real(text(git(primary,"rev-parse","--path-format=absolute","--git-common-dir")))===common&&origin(primary)===repo); const worktree=path.join(primary,"worktrees",id); if(registered){check(real(worktree)===worktree&&real(text(git(worktree,"rev-parse","--path-format=absolute","--git-common-dir")))===common); check(records(primary).filter(r=>r.worktree===worktree).length===1)} return {primary,common,worktree}}; const current=()=>real(text(git(process.cwd(),"rev-parse","--show-toplevel"))); const mapPath=(repo,root)=>path.join(root,"local-tmp",id,"evidence/runtime",repo,"phase-0",repo==="public"?"R-PUB":"R-PRI","execution-roots.json"); const ignored=(root,file)=>{check(fs.lstatSync(file).isFile()); git(root,"check-ignore","-q","--",file); check(git(root,"ls-files","--",file)==="")}; const validate=m=>{check(m&&typeof m==="object"&&!Array.isArray(m)&&Object.keys(m).sort().join(",")==="planId,privatePrimary,privateWorktree,publicPrimary,publicWorktree"); check(m.planId===id); for(const key of ["publicPrimary","privatePrimary","publicWorktree","privateWorktree"])check(typeof m[key]==="string"&&path.isAbsolute(m[key])&&!/[\r\n\0]/.test(m[key])); const a=discover(m.publicPrimary,"public",true),b=discover(m.privatePrimary,"private",true); check(a.primary!==b.primary&&a.common!==b.common&&a.primary===m.publicPrimary&&b.primary===m.privatePrimary&&a.worktree===m.publicWorktree&&b.worktree===m.privateWorktree); return m}; const load=expected=>{const repo=origin(process.cwd()); check(expected==="either"||repo===expected); const d=discover(process.cwd(),repo,true); check(current()===d.worktree); const file=mapPath(repo,d.worktree); ignored(d.worktree,file); const m=validate(JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file,"utf8"))); check(m[repo+"Worktree"]===current()); for(const other of ["public","private"]){const p=mapPath(other,m[other+"Worktree"]); ignored(m[other+"Worktree"],p); const peer=validate(JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(p,"utf8"))); check(Object.keys(m).every(k=>m[k]===peer[k]))} return m}; const d=discover(process.cwd(),"public",false); process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(d))'"'"')"; plan_primary="$(printf "%s" "$plan_identity" | rtk jq -r .primary)"; plan_worktree="$(printf "%s" "$plan_identity" | rtk jq -r .worktree)"; test ! -e "$plan_worktree"; if rtk git -C "$plan_primary" show-ref --verify --quiet refs/heads/adopt-beavernest-test-automation; then exit 1; fi; cd "$plan_primary"; claude --worktree adopt-beavernest-test-automation'
```

const name=u.pathname.replace(/^\//,"").replace(/\.git\/?$/,"").replace(/\/$/,""); check(["wahidyankf/ose-public","wahidyankf/ose-private"].includes(name)); return name.endsWith("ose-public")?"public":"private"}; const discover=(selected,repo,registered)=>{check(typeof selected==="string"&&selected.length>0&&!/[\r\n\0]/.test(selected)); const common=real(text(git(selected,"rev-parse","--path-format=absolute","--git-common-dir"))); check(path.basename(common)===".git"); const primary=path.dirname(common); check(real(text(git(primary,"rev-parse","--show-toplevel")))===primary&&real(text(git(primary,"rev-parse","--path-format=absolute","--git-common-dir")))===common&&origin(primary)===repo); const worktree=path.join(primary,"worktrees",id); if(registered){check(real(worktree)===worktree&&real(text(git(worktree,"rev-parse","--path-format=absolute","--git-common-dir")))===common); check(records(primary).filter(r=>r.worktree===worktree).length===1)} return {primary,common,worktree}}; check(Object.keys(m).every(k=>m[k]===peer[k]))} return m}; const d=discover(process.cwd(),"private",false); process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(d))'"'"')"; plan_primary="$(printf "%s" "$plan_identity" | rtk jq -r .primary)"; If a branch or path exists, stop. Inspect `rtk git worktree list --porcelain` and the branch ledger;
never force, delete, or reuse an unproven worktree. Never edit `ose-private` through its primary
checkout.

### Portable execution roots

`R-PUB:` and `R-PRI:` are location labels, not shell syntax. They mean the validated public
and private primary checkouts selected by the executor. Append the suffix after the colon to that
root before selecting a tool's working directory. Thus `R-PUB:worktrees/adopt-beavernest-test-automation`
selects the public execution worktree; no checkout basename or sibling-folder layout is assumed.

Before provisioning, select each existing checkout explicitly from the execution context. If its
location is unknown, ask the user; do not search unrelated directories or guess a sibling. The
commands below derive the primary root from Git's absolute common directory and verify the
canonical GitHub owner/repository for accepted SSH or HTTPS origins without printing the remote.
Use each repository's own terminal/working directory. Every command resolves its inputs again;
no exported root variable, previous shell, or shell startup file is required. Paths are passed as
quoted arguments, never interpolated into program source or regexes. Newline-containing paths are
rejected explicitly rather than silently misread.

After both Phase 0 worktrees exist, their existing ignored Phase 0 evidence trees each hold the
same five-field `execution-roots.json`: `planId`, `publicPrimary`, `privatePrimary`,
`publicWorktree`, and `privateWorktree`. The root setup actions below create and verify these
runtime-only files. Every cross-repository command validates both files, both repository origins,
the current checkout, and registered worktree/common-directory identities before doing work.
Missing, malformed, moved, mismatched, or same-clone maps stop the command; correct the selected
locations and rerun the root setup actions, never bypass validation. Maps contain raw local roots:
never commit them, copy them to sanitized exports, or put them in `implementation-notes.md`.
Cleanup independently rediscovers the primary checkout and does not load maps from a deleted tree.

## Executor Reading Contract

The intended executor is a junior engineer fresh from a bootcamp, with no professional work
experience and no repository or stack context, including no prior OSE, Nx, Rhino, or native-runner
knowledge.

- Perform actions in order. A later green aggregate does not prove an earlier checkbox.
- A valid `RED` fails for the named missing behavior. A crash or unrelated failure is invalid.
- `GREEN` adds only enough behavior to pass. `REFACTOR` changes structure without changing accepted
  behavior or diagnostics.
- Record every unexpected failure with command, exit code, first relevant error, root-cause fix, and
  successful rerun. Never weaken a gate.
- Use a Phase 0 ledger row only when it has exact paths, symbols, commands, expected output, and
  evidence location. Repair an incomplete row; never guess.
- Canonical Gherkin remains in [prd.md](./prd.md#acceptance-criteria); do not copy scenarios here.

## Execution Invariants

Code line coverage and behavior coverage are different gates. Each governed unit/integration line
slice is at least 99%. Gherkin/BDD requires integer `covered == total` for every feature, expanded
example, scenario, step, and applicable owner-adapter pair, with zero missing items and no rounding
or per-item exemption. Whole-layer inapplicability is decided before denominator construction.

Executable tests belong to exactly one `tests/unit/`, `tests/integration/`, or `tests/e2e/` root.
Dedicated E2E projects own `tests/e2e/` but share their product owner's corpus. A project-local
`package.json` remains only when Phase 0 names a direct consumer; convenience, task forwarding, and
Nx proxying are not consumers. Commands live directly in `project.json`.

Preserve production behavior/code, useful as-built C4 content, plan grilling, generic architecture
guidance, AyoKoding education outside `specs/`, and archived plans. Delete every DDD-specific
artifact in both active `specs/**` trees; do not retain or migrate it.

Before implementation in each delivery unit, estimate the diff. Treat 500 handwritten code/program
additions as a strong recommendation, not a hard cap. A larger natural cohesive seam may proceed
only when its record includes measured size, why the grouping is more reviewable, verifiable, and
revertible, split alternatives and why each was rejected, review proof, and recovery. The 1,000
documentation-addition and 300-total-file ceilings remain hard except for the sole, narrow
single-source other/document exception recorded below. Twenty hand-authored files is the default
review budget, not a reason to split a cohesive unit mechanically. Split first at a build-valid
test-layer, behavior-domain, project, or governance seam; a binding may exceed the default budget
only through the binding-specific record below.

### Binding-Specific File-Budget Exception Record

Natural seam is decisive. Do not use an exception for a broad inventory, a dynamic discovery result,
convenience, or a lower PR count. Before the first repository edit of a binding expected to exceed
20 hand-authored files (or the public planning budget of 17 implementation paths plus three
plan-state paths), add its exact record to this section and keep it through archival. The record must
state: binding; measured `C`, `O`, hand-authored-file, and total-file counts; the exact finite
allocation; its natural cohesive seam; the build-validity constraint; every viable rejected split and
why it is not independently reviewable, verifiable, or revertible; review proof; recovery; and the
matching PR-body disclosure. `PS-03`, `DB-04C`, and `DB-13A3` remeasure the same values and stop on
an absent, stale, incomplete, or mismatched record. No exception waives `O <= 1,000`, total files
`<= 300`, scope discipline, exact-head gates, or recovery. The sole narrow other/document exception
below is separate: it does not relax the file budget and it does not authorize any other binding.

### Single-Source Other/Document Exception Record

`D-O-PUB-AYO-CORPUS-WEB-TOOLS-COST-OF-LIVING` is the only delivery permitted to use the narrow
`O <= 1,100` rule. Its exact finite allocation is one existing non-generated source,
`specs/apps/ayokoding/behavior/ayokoding-www/gherkin/tools/cost-of-living-calculator.feature`,
and exactly one canonical non-generated behavior target,
`specs/apps/ayokoding/www/behaviors/ayokoding-www/gherkin/tools/cost-of-living-calculator.feature`;
the public delivery-state paths are the only additional admitted paths. The source has exactly
1,010 lines. The target preserves that one calculator behavior contract and must not include
navigation, another tool, a parent index, or a convenience edit.

The exception record before RED must state `Single-source other/document exception: required`, the
binding, `Measured other/document additions: 1010`, the exact source and target, the finite
allocation, the one-source/one-target semantic constraint, rejected viable splits, review proof,
recovery, the plan record, and the matching PR-body disclosure. `PS-03` and `DB-13A3` reject an
`O > 1,100` result, a source at or below 1,000 lines, a missing/mismatched record, more than one
behavior/contract target, or any added semantic scope. All other bindings retain `O <= 1,000`.

The Phase-0 `-le 17` and `-le 20` allocation assertions below express a default first split over
**source allocations**, not a false final-path count. A source-to-target move materially changes
both repository-relative paths and the public plan-state paths are admitted separately. If the
complete finite candidate fails a default, stop before materialization; prove whether a smaller
build-valid natural seam exists. Only after it is disproved may the named binding receive the full
record above and a matching checklist amendment. Never bypass an assertion in-place, merge
unrelated leaves, or treat a raw owner inventory as a cohesive delivery.

For every prospective and final size gate, canonical category `C` includes all non-generated,
non-Markdown source, test, script, configuration, data, and manifest additions; category `O`
includes Markdown and other document-type additions. Keep a separate detailed kind for review, but
sum the explicit `C`/`O` bucket rather than inferring from directories. Deleted lines and a
rename-verified pure move contribute zero additions. A wholly generated file uses the `generated`
bucket and is excluded only after its ownership declaration is verified; tests and configuration
never become line-exempt merely because they are not production source.

## Parallelization Model

The chosen orchestration budget is **N=3 delegated agents plus one coordinator**. That is the
repository default and is enough for one active writer, one read-only evidence/check specialist,
and one read-only verification specialist while the coordinator maintains the DAG and file ledger.
Only one agent writes a given repository at a time. Read-only work may overlap only when it does not
consume the same native runner, build cache, or generated output.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    P0[Phase 0: provision + baseline] --> D1[Phases 1-3: retire DDD]
    D1 --> F4[Phase 4: enforcement]
    F4 --> F5[Phase 5: specs + C4]
    F5 --> PUB[Public owners: phases 6-19]
    F5 --> PRI[Private owners: 7, 10B, 11B]
    PUB --> C20[Phases 20A-20B: closure]
    PRI --> C20
    C20 --> KC[Phase 21: Knowledge Capture]
    KC --> A22[Phase 22: audit + archive]
    A22 --> CLEAN[Terminal cleanup]
```

The public and private owner subgraphs are logically independent after Phase 5, but their heavy
operations are **repository-serial**: provision, run `rtk npm install`, converge the toolchain, build,
run native tests/coverage, validate generated bindings, and run final gates in `ose-public` first,
then `ose-private`. Do not overlap those operations across repositories. This default schedule needs
no machine-capacity exception. Within one repository, its single plan worktree and latest-main
dependency serialize delivery branches: finish the current boundary through merge/sync before
switching that worktree to the next declared branch. The evidence/check and verification agents may
inspect completed outputs concurrently while the writer is idle, but they never edit the same
branch.

Cleanup is the terminal `CLEAN` node. It is blocked by every public/private delivery, current-head
CI and leak review, surface gates, both closure nodes, Knowledge Capture, final audit/archive, merge
reachability, and terminal branch-ledger disposition. Therefore no worktree, branch, or evidence is
removed while another DAG node can still read it.

The 84 concrete delivery-unit PRs are the declared implementation catalog (62 public and 22
private). Eighteen prerequisite PRs have already established the portable delivery-record,
file-budget, preflight, Phase-0 reconciliation, private-Rhino parity, and narrow single-source
other/document rule seams. This physical-allocation amendment is the nineteenth prerequisite;
therefore the plan has **103 PRs** in total. Each prerequisite is a separate documentation/rule or
discovery seam; both members of every rule counterpart pair must merge before the first Phase 1
edit. The catalog change does not broaden product scope: it removes seven allocationless
coordination closeouts and replaces two Ayo test allocations with their eleven exact natural seams.

### Phase 0 Rhino parity discovery

Phase 0 compared the shared Rhino tree at both current `main` revisions. Of 99 shared paths, the
only intentionally private transition exception is the named DDD-retirement unit-test source, its
compile registration, and the resulting parity-manifest checksum difference. That exception remains
owned by the Phase 3 private Rhino delivery; it is not evidence that other shared paths may drift.

The comparison also found a stale private README whose content did not match the canonical public
F# documentation. `D-P0-PRI-RHINO-README-PARITY` corrects only that README and regenerates its
derived parity manifest. It is deliberately separate from Phase 3: documentation alignment and DDD
retirement change different behavior, can be reviewed independently, and can each be reverted
without recovering the other. Its PR must record the measured file accounting, the retained named
exception, the parity proof, and the independent revert path. This discovery does not complete the
declared-footprint resolution or authorize any split allocation.

### Phase 0 Rhino corpus discovery

The tracked Rhino corpus has 100 paths and 69 feature files in each repository. Four DDD paths are
reserved for Phase 3 retirement, leaving 96 non-retired corpus paths across the seven declared
Rhino corpus leaves. The previous reference to 76 was incorrect and is replaced by the executable
96-path rule below. The four-column allocation map records a unique target **and fragment** for each
source. For `CORPUS-METADATA`, the physical target is `specs/apps/rhino/cli/architecture.md` and its
fragment is `legacy-<source-path-stem>`, where the stem is the lower-case source path without its
extension and every maximal run of non-alphanumeric characters is replaced by one hyphen. The
corresponding Phase 7 delivery creates those named architecture sections; one physical document may
therefore receive several unique, independently traceable legacy sections.

The public/private corpus path sets match, but four private C4 documents have drifted from canonical
public content: `specs/apps/rhino/product/overview.md`,
`specs/apps/rhino/components/cli/component-cli.md`, `specs/apps/rhino/containers/container.md`, and
`specs/apps/rhino/system-context/context.md`. `D-P0-PRI-RHINO-C4-PARITY` aligns exactly those four
documents before source-hash parity is accepted. It is not combined with Phase 3 DDD retirement or
the README correction: each has a different review subject and a safe independent revert. This
discovery also does not complete the declared-footprint resolution or authorize split allocation.

The parent rows `D-P4-*`, `D-O-*-RHINO`, `D-O-PUB-AYO`, and `D-O-*-WEB-UI` are compact coordination
closeouts, not containers for their former implementation corpus. Their known implementation file
footprints already exceed the 20 hand-authored-file ceiling, so the following leaf lifecycle
bindings are mandatory before editing. Phase 0 writes the exact finite **source** allocation named
in the last column; one source path appears in exactly one leaf, and every leaf uses the full
concrete DB lifecycle in sequence. Its candidate then adds every distinct target, deletion, and
public plan-state path before the file budget is measured. Only after all leaves merge may the
parent closeout use its existing DB checklist for at most 17 implementation/configuration paths,
cross-leaf verification, and governance reconciliation; no implementation path may reappear there.
For public rows, the stated maximum is therefore not a final changed-file cap. The complete
candidate must fit the 20-file default or carry a named, finite file-budget natural-seam exception;
private candidates follow the same review rule with their ignored evidence model. Generated mirrors
remain in total-file accounting.

`D-P4-PUB-FIXTURES-A` owns four complete owner packets, hence 16 implementation paths and at most
19 hand-authored paths with its reserved plan-state files. Its former `O-PUB-FS-ENV` packet belongs
only to `D-O-PUB-FS-ENV`, which owns the complete eight-fixture bootstrap packet. `D-P4-PUB-FIXTURES-B`
and `D-P4-PUB-FIXTURES-C` each have a declared finite natural-seam exception: five complete owner
packets require exactly four independently selectable one-check fixture files each, hence 20
implementation paths and at most 23 hand-authored paths with the three reserved plan-state files.
Each exception must record the exact count, one-check schema/CLI constraint, rejected cross-owner
check split, review proof, recovery path, and PR disclosure; category O remains at most 1,000
additions and total files at most 300. Splitting B or C by check would replace its owner-cohort
delivery with cross-owner deliveries, change the 84-unit implementation catalog, and lose the
complete-owner-packet seam; it is not permitted.

The Phase 4 lists in [File-Impact Analysis](./tech-docs/file-impact-analysis.md#phase-4-finite-allocation)
are the exact finite allocation source for every formerly generic P4 path. The private
`D-P4-PRI-POLICY-PARITY` list intentionally contains all 29 named BDD, coverage, layout, and
manifest policy fixtures plus its nine shared implementation/test/wiring paths. It is the single
private proof that the completed public foundation is byte-identical across the shared Rhino tree;
it must carry a named 38-path file-budget exception. Splitting it would leave each private commit
unable to prove the required complete shared-foundation parity, so the exception records that
build-validity, the rejected partial-parity alternative, exact allocation, review proof, recovery,
and PR-body disclosure. The private fixture manifest is ignored delivery evidence, not a
hand-authored repository path.

### Physical Move-Pair Reconciliation

The old fixed source-allocation maxima did not measure a move as the reviewed delivery sees it:
the retiring source, canonical target, and public delivery-state files are all distinct paths. The
physical resolver records every source-to-target pair before materialization. A binding with more
than 20 complete candidate paths must retain its named semantic owner, test root, or corpus leaf
when a smaller allocation would either split one build-valid test root, leave its canonical
behavior/C4 index half-migrated, or separate a behavior contract from its source/target pair. Its
file-budget record is therefore mandatory; it is never a blanket owner-inventory exception.

The reconciliation keeps the existing owner and corpus seams. It does not create count-driven
micro-PRs. The substantive seam corrections are Ayo's former mixed navigation/tools leaf and the
two oversized Ayo test leaves. Navigation, ordinary tools, and the calculator contract are
independently reviewable. The calculator is further isolated because it is the only source above
1,000 document lines. The test correction uses existing backend/frontend harness, application,
project, and feature-domain seams; it does not split individual tests merely to reduce a count.

| Catalog change                                  |             Source allocation | Complete-candidate decision                                                              | Reason and required evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------: | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `D-O-PUB-AYO-CORPUS-WEB-NAVIGATION`             |         9 source/target pairs | named file-budget record                                                                 | One navigation behavior corpus; splitting individual redirect contracts would leave its navigation index and behavior set non-atomic.                                                                                                            |
| `D-O-PUB-AYO-CORPUS-WEB-TOOLS`                  |         3 source/target pairs | within default unless the measured candidate adds an independently required control path | Three ordinary tool documents only; calculator excluded.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `D-O-PUB-AYO-CORPUS-WEB-TOOLS-COST-OF-LIVING`   |          1 source/target pair | single-source O record; normal file budget                                               | Exact one-source/one-target calculator contract; no unrelated tool or navigation file.                                                                                                                                                           |
| `D-O-PUB-AYO-UNIT`                              |              170 source moves | eight bounded test-harness, platform, and feature-domain leaves                          | The former 340-path candidate violates the non-waivable 300-file ceiling; exact replacements are legacy backend/frontend steps, application platform, AI benchmark, app-shell/navigation, content/i18n/search, cost-of-living, and course-paths. |
| `D-O-PUB-AYO-INTEGRATION-E2E`                   |               39 source moves | three project-bound leaves                                                               | The application integration suite and the independently buildable backend/frontend Playwright projects are distinct first project seams.                                                                                                         |
| Existing named owner, test-root, or corpus leaf | resolver-defined finite pairs | named file-budget record only when complete candidate exceeds 20                         | Preserve the declared build-valid owner/test-root or canonical corpus seam; record exact counts, rejected smaller seams, review proof, recovery, plan location, and PR disclosure.                                                               |

The record name is `natural-seam-exception.md` in the binding's ignored delivery evidence, while
this section is the durable plan record. Every record must match the current candidate exactly;
`PS-03`, `DB-04C`, and `DB-13A3` reject a stale or more-broad record. A move pair is not an
addition exemption: category `C`/`O`, all paths, the 300-file ceiling, and current-head reviews
remain measured.

Each leaf branch basename is the parent basename plus the lowercase final suffix, for example
`test-contract-web-ui-unit`. Execute leaves top-to-bottom within their coordination group and
merge/sync each before creating the next leaf from current `origin/main`; then create the compact
parent closeout branch from current `origin/main`. The Phase 0 split gate must prove each
coordination group's source union is exhaustive, pairwise disjoint, and within its numeric
allocation. It may reduce a conservative addition estimate, but it may not merge leaves, invent a
different binding, defer a known split to runtime, or move a leaf implementation path into the
parent closeout.

For every public group, normalize the frozen path allocation before its first edit: executable test
and runner paths stay in their named test-layer leaf; fixture/data paths move only to that group's
named fixture or corpus leaf; C4/index/README paths move only to `CORPUS-METADATA`; rule and binding
source paths move only to `GOVERNANCE` or `CORPUS-GOVERNANCE`; direct target and manifest paths move
only to `CONTRACT`. The exact before/after assignment is recorded in the group's Phase 0 allocation,
and the union must remain identical. If these finite named seams cannot make every public allocation
at most 17 paths, stop and amend the plan with a new build-valid lifecycle binding before editing;
never choose a split while executing a delivery.

Every unaffected main-table row is one PR. Phases 20B–22 remain one final public delivery unit:
archival occurs on that branch before final review and merge. There is no separate archival PR.

## Controlled Runbook RP — Rules Propagation per Repository

Apply every `RP-*` action separately to every finite binding below. Track `01` through `09`, the
four independent `10A` through `10D` actions, then `11` and `12` for each concrete binding; one
repository's evidence never satisfies another.

| Binding                     | Repository      | Subject set                               | Phase |
| --------------------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----- |
| `RP-P1-PUB`                 | `R-PUB`         | retire OrganicLever DDD specs/enforcement | 1     |
| `RP-P2-PUB`                 | `R-PUB`         | retire OSE DDD specs/enforcement          | 2     |
| `RP-P3-PUB` / `RP-P3-PRI`   | each named repo | retire shared DDD machinery               | 3     |
| `RP-P4-PUB` / `RP-P4-PRI`   | each named repo | registry, 99%, BDD, layout, manifests     | 4     |
| `RP-P5-PUB` / `RP-P5-PRI`   | each named repo | specs corpus and C4 lifecycle             | 5     |
| `RP-OWNER-<owner-id>`       | owner repo      | existing-rule application reconciliation  | 6–19  |
| `RP-P20-PUB` / `RP-P20-PRI` | each named repo | final test/CI contract                    | 20    |

- **Procedure** `RP-01` — open
  `repo-governance/workflows/rules/rules-propagation.md`; record its current SHA and every linked
  mandatory step in `<phase>/<repo-id>/rules-propagation.md`. Stop if absent or unreadable.
- **Procedure** `RP-02` — write one falsifiable rule sentence, pass condition, violation condition, and
  subject inventory for the binding; acceptance: no subject is only an aspiration.
- **Procedure** `RP-03` — run the workflow's conflict scan against canonical governance, `AGENTS.md`,
  `repo-config.yml`, machinery, `.claude/`, generated bindings, project targets, hooks, CI, and
  indexes; record conflict, precedence, and same-layer supersession for every match before edit.
- **Procedure** `RP-04` — choose canonical placement and list every obsolete/contradictory surface to
  evict; stop on unresolved precedence instead of retaining two active versions.
- **Procedure** `RP-05` — reconcile canonical prose, config, enforcement, and discoverability indexes.
  For owner application, record `no canonical change` plus evidence per surface, not a silent skip.
- **Procedure** `RP-06` — apply the binding-specific config/enforcement disposition. A foundation
  binding names its exact fixture and symbol; a deletion-only or owner no-change binding records
  why a new fixture is inapplicable and cites the exact deletion or existing owner fixture proof.
- **Procedure** `RP-07` — update canonical `.claude/` agents/skills when required; never hand-edit
  `.agents/`, `.opencode/`, or `.codex/` mirrors.
- **Procedure** `RP-08` — reconcile `project.json`, root scripts, hooks, workflows, and indexes; use the
  required three-way enforcement disposition `enforced`, `advisory-only with reason`, or
  `not enforceable with reason`, plus exact mechanism/proof where enforced.
- **Procedure** `RP-09` — run `rtk npm run generate:bindings`; acceptance: exit zero and only generated
  mirrors change.
- **Procedure** `RP-10A` — run `rtk npm run sync:dry-run`; acceptance: exit zero and no drift.
- **Procedure** `RP-10B` — run the repository-specific generated-binding validation command recorded
  in Phase 0; acceptance: exit zero.
- **Procedure** `RP-10C` — execute the first strict rules-quality-gate validation; acceptance: one
  audit UUID and zero threshold findings.
- **Procedure** `RP-10D` — without an intervening edit, execute the second strict validation;
  acceptance: a different audit UUID, the same source head, and zero threshold findings.
- **Procedure** `RP-11` — run Phase 0-recorded config, governance, Markdown, link, README-map,
  directory-map, and focused subject validators; fix every failure and rerun.
- **Procedure** `RP-12` — complete manifest and final status with inventory; conflict/precedence/
  supersession; placement/eviction; canonical/config/enforcement/index changes; three-way
  enforcement dispositions; bindings; rules-quality-gate results; and sibling-repository
  obligation. Every row and required sibling binding is terminal; diff matches ledger.

## Controlled Runbook OM — One Owner Migration

Execute every `OM-*` action for every `D-O-*` binding. Replace `<owner-id>` only with its stable ID;
exact paths, symbols, target commands, expected failures, and evidence files come from that complete
Phase 0 row. Track `<binding>-OM-01`, the prospective `<binding>-OM-18A` through `OM-18C` trio,
then `<binding>-OM-02` through `<binding>-OM-17` as separate tasks; the apparently non-numeric
placement is deliberate because size feasibility must be proved before the first RED edit.

- **Procedure** `OM-01` — reread the owner row and run each recorded baseline; acceptance: all exit zero.
  Stop and repair Phase 0 if a required field is blank.
- **Procedure** `OM-02 RED-layout` — create the bounded owner `layout-misplaced.json` fixture and run
  the exact Phase 4 `test-contract validate --owner ... --check layout --fixture ...` leaf. Exit 1
  must name the owner and misplaced/overlapping path; exit 2 or an unrelated crash is invalid.

  wire the normal no-fixture layout target in the exact `project.json`, and require exit 0.
- **Procedure** `OM-04 REFACTOR-layout` — normalize only runner globs/imports and prove the same test
  count plus a green layout target.
- **Procedure** `OM-05 RED-coverage` — create the bounded `coverage-98.json` fixture and run the same
  Phase 4 leaf with `--check coverage`; require exit 1 naming owner, expected 99, and actual 98.
- **Procedure** `OM-06 GREEN-coverage` — add behavior-valued tests, set every applicable native line
  threshold to at least 99, and run the real no-fixture owner coverage target.
- **Procedure** `OM-07 REFACTOR-coverage` — deduplicate only coverage setup and prove unchanged
  numerator/denominator, exclusions, outputs, and policy diagnostics.
- **Procedure** `OM-08 RED-BDD` — create the bounded `bdd-missing-step.json` fixture and run the Phase
  4 leaf with `--check bdd`; require exit 1 with owner/adapter/item and integer totals.
- **Procedure** `OM-09 GREEN-BDD` — add or move real owner bindings until every applicable integer

- **Procedure** `OM-10 REFACTOR-BDD` — deduplicate only binding/report helpers and prove unchanged

- **Procedure** `OM-11 RED-manifest` — create the bounded `manifest-proxy.json` fixture and run the

- **Procedure** `OM-13 REFACTOR-manifest` — remove duplicated forwarding/config, reinstall, and prove

validate-mapping --project <exact-project> --require-state <identity|redirected>` plus specs/C4

- **Procedure** `OM-17 verification` — run every applicable owner build/test/coverage/BDD/layout/
  manifest/specs/C4 command and require all checks green. Read the repository's frozen

frozen="$phase0/registry/registry-project-closure.sha"; out="local-tmp/adopt-beavernest-test-automation/evidence/runtime/$side/owners/$binding/registry-closure"; projects="$out/projects.txt"; proof="$out/verified-projects.tsv"; legacy_all="$out/legacy-all.tsv"; canonical_all="$out/canonical-all.tsv"; test -s "$closure"; test "$(rtk git hash-object "$closure")" = "$(rtk tr -d "\n" < "$frozen")"; rtk mkdir -p "$out"; rtk awk -F "$(rtk printf "\t")" -v b="$binding" "\$4 == b { print \$1 }" "$closure" | rtk sort -u > "$projects"; for snapshot in "$legacy_all" "$canonical_all"; do test -s "$snapshot"; rtk awk -F "$(rtk printf "\t")" "NF != 4 || \$1 == \"\" { exit 1 }; { if (seen[\$1]++) exit 1 }" "$snapshot"; done; rtk diff -u <(rtk cut -f1 "$closure" | rtk sort -u) <(rtk cut -f1 "$legacy_all" | rtk sort -u); rtk diff -u <(rtk cut -f1 "$legacy_all" | rtk sort -u) <(rtk cut -f1 "$canonical_all" | rtk sort -u); rtk apps/rhino-cli/scripts/rhino-bin.sh test-contract registry compare --legacy "$legacy_all" --canonical "$canonical_all" > "$out/all-projects.compare.txt"; rtk awk -F "$(rtk printf "\t")" -v p="$project" "\$1 == p { print }" "$canonical_all" > "$canonical"; test "$(rtk wc -l < "$legacy" | rtk tr -d " ")" -eq 1; test "$(rtk wc -l < "$canonical" | rtk tr -d " ")" -eq 1; rtk apps/rhino-cli/scripts/rhino-bin.sh test-contract registry validate-mapping --project "$project" --require-state verified > "$out/$project.mapping.txt"; rtk apps/rhino-cli/scripts/rhino-bin.sh test-contract registry compare --legacy "$legacy" --canonical "$canonical" > "$out/$project.compare.txt"; rtk awk -F "$(rtk printf "\t")" "NF != 4 || \$1 == \"\" || \$2 != \"verified\" || \$3 == \"\" || \$4 == \"\" { exit 1 }; { if (seen[\$1]++) exit 1 }" "$proof"; rtk diff -u "$projects" <(rtk cut -f1 "$proof" | rtk sort -u)'`. The snapshot grammar is exact: legacy accepts only `--source legacy --output`, while canonical additionally consumes `--project-list-from`; neither form accepts `--project`. OM-17 takes each repository-wide legacy snapshot once, derives the canonical full preservation snapshot once, proves both full sets equal the frozen closure, and only then extracts exactly one row per binding project mechanically. Acceptance is one unique extracted legacy row, canonical row, and proof row per exact closure project, no missing/extra project at either the repository or binding scope, the same normalized owner/behavior/runtime identity on both sides, current canonical paths in the map, frozen legacy fields unchanged, and all owner gates green. Restore every selected pre-OM-14 canonical row/map together on any failure; do not verify only the owner while leaving its delegates or behavior-free steward rows pending. This closure attachment is part of every concrete `<binding>-OM-17` checkbox below; its named owner commands do not complete the checkbox until the binding-specific project set, full-snapshot checks, per-project proof TSV, exact count, and no-missing/no-extra comparisons above all pass.

  eight-field candidate at `$raw_root/prospective-current.tsv`:

- **Procedure** `PS-03 prospective-gate` — calculate category C from ignored candidate fields 4/6,
  category O from fields 4/6, hand-authored count from field 5, and path count from all rows. Run
  `rtk bash -lc 'test -s "$candidate"; code="$(rtk awk -F "$(rtk printf "\\t")" "\$4 == \"C\" { n += \$6 }; END { print n + 0 }" "$candidate")"; other="$(rtk awk -F "$(rtk printf "\\t")" "\$4 == \"O\" { n += \$6 }; END { print n + 0 }" "$candidate")"; hand="$(rtk awk -F "$(rtk printf "\\t")" "\$5 == \"hand-authored\" { n++ }; END { print n + 0 }" "$candidate")"; files="$(rtk wc -l < "$candidate" | rtk tr -d " ")"; test "$files" -gt 0; test "$other" -le 1000; test "$files" -le 300; file_exception=0; if test "$hand" -gt 20; then file_exception=1; fi; if test "$side" = public && test "$files" -gt 20; then file_exception=1; fi; exception_required=0; if test "$code" -gt 500 || test "$file_exception" -eq 1; then exception_required=1; fi; status="within recommendation and default file budget"; if test "$exception_required" -eq 1; then test -s "$exception"; for label in "Natural-seam exception:" "Binding: $binding" "Measured Category C additions: $code" "Natural cohesive seam:" "Split alternative:" "Why split was rejected:" "Review proof:" "Recovery:"; do rtk rg -F -q -- "$label" "$exception" || exit 1; done; ! rtk rg -n "pending|unknown|TBD|TODO" "$exception"; if test "$file_exception" -eq 1; then status="file-budget natural-seam exception recorded"; for label in "File-budget exception: required" "Measured other/document additions: $other" "Measured hand-authored files: $hand" "Measured total files: $files" "Exact finite allocation:" "Build-validity constraint:" "Plan record:" "PR body disclosure:"; do rtk rg -F -q -- "$label" "$exception" || exit 1; done; elif test "$code" -gt 500; then status="code natural-seam exception recorded"; fi; else test ! -e "$exception"; fi; rtk printf "Binding: %s\\nSize status: %s\\nCategory C additions: %s / 500 recommendation\\nOther/document additions: %s / 1000 hard ceiling\\nHand-authored files: %s / 20 default budget\\nTotal files: %s / 300 hard ceiling\\nFile-budget exception: %s\\nIgnored candidate: %s\\n" "$binding" "$status" "$code" "$other" "$hand" "$files" "$file_exception" "$candidate" > "$gate"; test -s "$gate"'`.
  Expect the hard `O <= 1,000` and total-file `<= 300` ceilings green for this binding, regardless
  of rows retained for earlier units. `C > 500` requires the measured cohesive seam, rejected split
  alternatives, reviewability/verifiability/revertibility proof, and recovery. Exceeding the default
  20-file budget requires the exact finite allocation, build-validity constraint, rejected viable
  splits, review proof, recovery, plan record, and PR-body disclosure. Every concrete
  `*-PRE-01..03`, `*-EARLY-01..03`, or owner `OM-18A..C` executes `PS-01..03` with its exact paths;
  no later gate recreates its branch.

- **Procedure** `PS-03S single-source-other-document-gate` — This procedure replaces `PS-03` only
  for `D-O-PUB-AYO-CORPUS-WEB-TOOLS-COST-OF-LIVING`. Use the same candidate, gate, and exception
  paths as `PS-03`, calculate `C`, `O`, hand-authored count, and total files identically, then
  enforce `O <= 1,100` and total files `<= 300`; require the ordinary natural-seam record if
  `C > 500`. Require exactly one candidate source
  row with the existing calculator path, exactly one candidate target row with the canonical
  calculator target path, no other behavior/contract source or target, and a source line count of
  exactly 1,010. Require the complete record named in [Single-Source Other/Document Exception
  Record](#single-source-otherdocument-exception-record), reject `pending`, `unknown`, `TBD`, or
  `TODO`, and write the measured facts and `Single-source other/document exception: 1` to the
  ignored gate and PR body. A source/target mismatch, extra semantic row, missing PR disclosure,
  or any other binding invoking this procedure is a stop condition.

## Controlled Runbook DB — Complete PR Lifecycle

Apply `DB-01` through `DB-16` to every unaffected Delivery Boundaries row, every mandatory leaf
lifecycle row, and every compact parent closeout except Phase 0. Track each action with its exact
`D-*` binding; a parent action or artifact never satisfies a leaf action. `DB-14` is an explicit
merge gate; do not absorb, retag, or script it.

- **Procedure** `DB-01` — run focused commands plus
  `rtk nx affected -t build,typecheck,lint,test:quick` and applicable
  `test:integration,test:e2e`; acceptance: all exit zero.
- **Procedure** `DB-02` — run recorded specs, exact BDD, config, bindings, Markdown, Prettier, links,
  README, maps, Mermaid/C4, workflow, and rules-manifest gates; all applicable commands exit zero.
- **Procedure** `DB-03` — run `rtk git status --short --untracked-files=all`, `rtk git diff --check`,
  and a union of committed, unstaged, staged, and untracked paths. Record the exact `origin/main`
  SHA; materialize the complete union as `delivery-paths.txt` and separately derive
  `stage-paths.txt` from only unstaged, staged, and untracked paths. Reconcile every path and prove
  no secret, `.env*`, proxy, unchecked exclusion, or unintended behavior.
- **Procedure** `DB-04` — run applicable UI/API/deploy/live gates from Phase 0. `Not applicable` requires
  complete committed-plus-working-tree proof of no affected public/deployment surface. Create the
  delivery's complete `pr-body.md`, refresh both path files, and prove the stageable set is a subset
  of the complete delivery ledger before staging.
- **Procedure** `DB-05` — after explicit authorization for this named change set, stage only
  `stage-paths.txt`; never attempt to re-stage committed-only ledger paths. Create the fewest
  build-valid Conventional Commits; staged diff and subjects match one unit.
- **Procedure** `DB-06` — rerun pre-push gates against the committed head. Store all after-stage and
  after-commit outputs in the repository's ignored runtime root, then require a clean tracked head.
  If a gate changes tracked files, obtain authorization for the correction and restart at `DB-01`.
- **Procedure** `DB-07` — push only the delivery branch; open/update one PR to `main`; record URL, base,
  `expected_head=$(rtk git rev-parse HEAD)`, cost/benefit, counts, recovery, and evidence.
- **Procedure** `DB-08` — run `rtk gh pr view --json headRefOid,baseRefOid,baseRefName`; acceptance:
  the recorded head matches `HEAD`, base name is `main`, and `baseRefOid` equals the exact
  pre-commit `origin/main` SHA in `base-sha.txt`. Any mismatch stops review.
- **Procedure** `DB-09` — poll `.github/workflows/pr-quality-gate.yml` every two minutes without
  `gh run watch`; `Quality gate` must be green for exact head/base. A fix restarts at `DB-07`.
- **Procedure** `DB-10` — invoke one authenticated `pr-leak-review` for exact head/base and record clean
  `pass`; a changed head invalidates it and requires one replacement pass.
- **Procedure** `DB-11` — run every applicable finite UI/API, accessibility, deploy/live, Rhino parity,
  or private-infra surface gate; record tool/command, surface, observation, and head. Record
  evidence-backed `not applicable` for all others.
- **Procedure** `DB-12` — for the final public unit, archive the plan before final review; otherwise prove
  the unit's plan/evidence references are current.
- **Procedure** `DB-13` — from a clean head, create one no-renames whole-delivery numstat/path
  manifest; classify every unique file by detailed kind and explicit canonical `C`/`O`/`generated`
  bucket; measure the 500 category-`C` recommendation; require its exact natural-seam record when
  exceeded; hard-enforce 1,000 category-`O` additions and 300 total files; and require the exact
  binding-specific file-budget natural-seam record if hand-authored files exceed the default 20.
  Read the final diff, prove no independent scope is bundled, and repeat
  `DB-08`–`DB-11` if head changed; all CI/leak/surface evidence must refer to one head/base.
- **Procedure** `DB-14` — merge the PR through the sanctioned GitHub channel only after `DB-13` is true.
- **Procedure** `DB-15` — run `rtk git fetch origin main`; capture `headRefOid`, `baseRefOid`,
  `mergeCommit`, and `state`; compare head/base to the reviewed `DB-13C` identity; prove the merge
  SHA is reachable from `origin/main`; and write the verified head/base/merge/terminal state to the
  branch ledger.
- **Procedure** `DB-16` — create/switch the next declared branch from current `origin/main`, run
  `rtk git status --short`, and rerun its baseline; acceptance: clean/green before next phase.

### Terminal Worktree Cleanup

Cleanup runs from each validated primary checkout, never from the execution worktree being
removed. The context action emits the primary location only into ignored runtime evidence; select
that resolved runtime location as the next tool working directory because a subshell cannot change
the caller's working directory.
On a later fresh-shell resume, select the already verified `R-PUB:` or `R-PRI:` primary location
again; none of the removal/prune commands needs an inherited root variable or a surviving map.

The existing post-archive evidence family continues in each primary checkout's ignored
`local-tmp/adopt-beavernest-test-automation/evidence/runtime/<public|private>/post-archive/terminal-cleanup/`
directory, outside the execution tree. `before.json` is the immediate pre-removal inventory;
`after-removal.json` and `after-prune.json` prove exact preservation of every unrelated porcelain
record. Keep these raw local paths ignored. A `rules-update` tree is preserved if actually present
in `before.json`; an already-absent authoring tree is neither required nor recreated. If an unrelated
record changes, stop and investigate without deleting, restoring, or silently rebaselining it.
